meta.titre: Complete sentences with contextually appropriate vocabulary of one's own

sections.contenu_markdown: Unlike a multiple-choice question, a "fill in with your own word" task has no list of options to fall back on - the whole sentence itself becomes the only clue, and reading it carefully is the only reliable strategy.

items: Basic sentence structure to identify the missing word's grammatical role (noun, verb, adjective)
A working vocabulary of common everyday topics (health, school, family)

sections.titre: Method for filling a blank with your own word
sections.contenu_markdown:
To fill a blank correctly with a word of your own choice, first read the WHOLE sentence (not just the words immediately before the blank) to understand its overall meaning. Then identify what GRAMMATICAL CATEGORY is expected at that position (noun, verb, adjective, adverb) from the surrounding words (an article "a/the" before the blank usually signals a noun; an adverb like "very" usually signals an adjective).

Finally, choose a word that is both grammatically correct AND makes logical sense in context. Several different words are usually acceptable, as long as they satisfy both conditions - there is rarely only one "correct" answer expected.
sections.formule_principale: \text{Correct answer} = \text{grammatically correct category} + \text{logical meaning in context}

sections.enonce_markdown: Complete: "After the long journey, the travellers were extremely ……………. and went straight to bed."

etapes.action: Read the whole sentence for context
etapes.justification: "long journey" and "went straight to bed" give strong clues about the meaning needed.
etapes.resultat_markdown: Context: a long journey, followed by going to bed immediately

etapes.justification: The adverb "extremely" before the blank signals that an ADJECTIVE is expected.
The word must describe a state consistent with a long journey and going to bed immediately.

sections.conclusion_markdown: "Tired" or "exhausted" both fit perfectly: they are adjectives (matching the position after "extremely") and logically explain why the travellers went straight to bed after a long journey.

items.erreur_markdown: Choosing a word based only on the few words immediately before the blank, without reading the rest of the sentence.
items.pourquoi_faux: The full meaning and logic of the sentence often only becomes clear once the whole sentence is read, including what comes AFTER the blank - stopping early risks missing an essential clue.
items.correction_markdown: Always read the entire sentence, including what follows the blank, before choosing a word.

items.erreur_markdown: Proposing a word of the wrong grammatical category (e.g. a noun where an adjective is clearly expected).
items.pourquoi_faux: Even a word that fits the general topic will be marked wrong if it does not match the grammatical slot required by the sentence's structure (article, adverb, verb agreement).
items.correction_markdown: Always double-check that the proposed word's grammatical category matches what the sentence structure requires at that position.

items.enonce_markdown: Complete: "The nurse gave the injured man first ………………. before the ambulance arrived."
items.solution_markdown: aid — "first aid" is a fixed expression meaning emergency treatment given before proper medical help arrives.

items.enonce_markdown: Complete: "Because of the heavy rain, the farmers lost most of their ………………. this year."
items.solution_markdown: harvest / crops — a noun referring to what farmers grow and collect, logically lost due to heavy rain.

items.enonce_markdown: Explain why the sentence "The teacher was very disappointed because the students had studied so ……………. for the exam" requires an ADVERB rather than an adjective, and propose a suitable word.
items.solution_markdown: The blank follows the verb "had studied" and the intensifier "so", both of which modify a VERB, not a noun: an adverb is therefore required to describe HOW the students studied, not WHAT they are. A suitable adverb is "little" or "badly" (e.g. "studied so little"), consistent with the teacher's disappointment expressed earlier in the sentence.

items_markdown: Always read the whole sentence, not just the words right before the blank.
Identify the grammatical category expected (noun, verb, adjective, adverb) from surrounding clues.
Choose a word that is both grammatically correct and logically consistent with the sentence's meaning.
Several different words can be acceptable as long as both conditions are satisfied.
